sense: people born at about the same time; the span of a lifetime

terms.gloss: a generation; an age, a time
evidence: Cic. Sen. 31: tertiam jam enim aetātem hominum vidēbat
Hor. Carm. 3.6.46: aetās parentum, pejor avīs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a space of time, an age, generation; nostrā aetāte, in our time (Quint. 1.4.20).

terms.gloss: a generation of people; a lifetime, an age
evidence: Cic. Sen. 24 (Caecilius): serit arborēs quae alterī saeclō prōsint
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: the human race living in a particular age, a generation, the times; also a century (see century). Saeclum is the shortened form of old Latin and of poetry.

terms.gloss: people of one’s own age: one’s generation
terms.grammar: noun, third declension, plural: the adjective aequālis used as a noun
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 48: Ō amīce, salvē, atque aequālis
terms.comment: One’s contemporaries, those born about when one was.
Lewis & Short: coming generations, descendants, posterity.
Christian Latin, after the Greek of the Gospels; classically a begetting (Pliny).

phrases.latin: serit arborēs quae alterī saeclō prōsint
phrases.english: he plants trees to be of use to the next generation

phrases.latin: aetās parentum, pejor avīs, tulit nōs nēquiōrēs, mox datūrōs prōgeniem vitiōsiōrem
phrases.english: our parents’ generation, worse than our grandparents’, bore us, worse still, and we shall soon have children more wicked yet

phrases.latin: Tertiam jam enim aetātem hominum vidēbat
phrases.english: for he was already seeing a third generation of men
